<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915124_theRebbe_182" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915124_theRebbe_182__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header information for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Toldos,</t>
    <t s="2">Erev Rosh Chodesh Kislev 5727</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions why the verse mentions both finding a hundredfold and being blessed by G-d, implying they are separate matters, and asks what the unspecified blessing was.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And Yitzchak sowed in that land and found in that year a hundredfold, and G-d blessed him."</t>
    <t s="1">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">From the fact that it says "and G-d blessed him" after "he found... a hundredfold,"</t>
    <t s="3">it implies that "and G-d blessed him" is an additional matter beyond his finding a hundredfold,</t>
    <t s="4">and an explanation is needed as to why it says "and He blessed him" without specifying with what He blessed him.</t>
    <t s="5">Also, it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="6">Behold, even this finding of a hundredfold</t>
    <t s="7">(one hundred times what was estimated)</t>
    <t s="8">is not according to the ways of nature, but rather the blessing of G-d,</t>
    <t s="9">and on the other hand,</t>
    <t s="10">also the blessing of "and G-d blessed him" that came after the finding of the hundredfold is that Yitzchak was blessed with this blessing</t>
    <t s="11">("and G-d blessed him"),</t>
    <t s="12">and nevertheless, the finding of the hundredfold is attributed by the verse to Yitzchak</t>
    <t s="13">("and he found... a hundredfold"),</t>
    <t s="14">and regarding the blessing with which Yitzchak was blessed after he found the hundredfold, it says "and G-d blessed him."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the two aspects in the verse—finding a hundredfold and being blessed—relate to the produce, while the subsequent verse about Yitzchak growing great refers to his entire being.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing what the verse continues,</t>
    <t s="2">"And the man grew great, and he went on growing until he became very great,"</t>
    <t s="3">that through "and Yitzchak sowed, etc." there was a growth in Yitzchak himself,</t>
    <t s="4">"and the man grew great, etc."</t>
    <t s="5">For the two matters in the verse "and Yitzchak sowed, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="6">"and he found... a hundredfold" and "and G-d blessed him,"</t>
    <t s="7">are regarding the produce,</t>
    <t s="8">"and he found a hundredfold" is an extraordinary increase in the produce itself,</t>
    <t s="9">"and G-d blessed him" is that he sold his produce at a high price.</t>
    <t s="10">And although all matters of the Patriarchs</t>
    <t s="11">[and particularly the matters of the Patriarchs mentioned in the Torah]</t>
    <t s="12">are spiritual matters,</t>
    <t s="13">from this it is understood that in Yitzchak's produce there was</t>
    <t s="14">(also)</t>
    <t s="15">a spiritual matter,</t>
    <t s="16">and the two matters of "and he found a hundredfold" and "and G-d blessed him" are also regarding the spiritual aspect of Yitzchak's produce,</t>
    <t s="17">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="18">they are only regarding a particular matter</t>
    <t s="19">(produce).</t>
    <t s="20">And in the subsequent verse it adds that through the service of "and Yitzchak sowed, etc." there was also growth in his entire being,</t>
    <t s="21">"and the man grew great, etc."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
